stem: In the two-link diagram, which assignment matches the frame origins and x-axis directions?

options.text: Frames0 and1 originate at the base, with x0 horizontal and x1 along link1; frame2 originates at the elbow with x2 along link2, and frame3 is at the tip aligned with frame2
Frame1 originates at the elbow along link1; frame2 is at the tip along link2; frame3 is at the base
Frames0,1,2 and3 all originate at the base; only their labels change
Frame1 originates at the base along link1; frame2 is at the elbow but its x2 remains horizontal, and frame3 points along link1

assumptions: Use the frame assignment drawn in this source example, not an arbitrary alternative convention.

stem: The source notes that even a2-DOF closed-form torque equation is lengthy; why can the recursive method still be useful for a6-DOF robot?

options.text: It makes all six joint torques equal so only one formula is needed
It removes the dependence of torque on joint velocity and acceleration
It guarantees that every6-DOF expanded symbolic expression is shorter than the2-DOF one
It evaluates linkwise motion and force recursions without requiring a fully expanded symbolic torque formula
